questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to Canada, and because I love nature, Victoria seemed like the perfect destination. The city is close to the ocean, mountains, and lots of beautiful nature. I also liked that it is located on Vancouver Island, a bit away from the bigger cities, while still being a small and cosy city.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I can highly recommend the University of Victoria. I had a very positive experience studying there and really enjoyed my time at the university. If I had the opportunity, I would definitely choose to spend another semester there.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy to find the information I needed upon arrival. The university was very helpful and informative, and I felt very welcome from the beginning.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We received a lot of information about everything we needed to know when we arrived, and there were plenty of opportunities to ask questions if we were unsure about anything or needed help.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was fairly easy to find off-campus housing. There are several Facebook groups where students can look for accommodation, and many of my friends found housing this way, which seemed to work well. I lived in a house in the Gordon Head area, which I can definitely recommend. It is close to the university, the ocean, and nature, while still being only around 30 minutes from downtown.
We started looking for housing quite early and found a place through Airbnb in January. If you are travelling with other students from your home university, it can be a good idea to look for a larger house that you can share.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living off campus was a great experience. It gave me the opportunity to experience everyday life in the local area, and living with roommates created a nice and social atmosphere.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Overall, the registration process was quite extensive and demanding, as there was a lot of information that we had to find ourselves. It was quite confusing and stressful, so overall, the process could have been better organized and made more straightforward for students

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could contact the university by email if you needed help, and they were very helpful and responsive.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was very successful and managed to register for all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Set aside plenty of time and start well in advance, as the registration process can be quite demanding. Make sure you are aware of the different deadlines and when the courses take place.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Overall, I found the academic level slightly lower than at UCPH. The courses generally covered the topics more broadly, whereas at UCPH I feel that we tend to go into more depth. However, the courses were still very interesting and challenging.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very similar to UCPH. There were both lectures and smaller class sessions, but the teaching mainly consisted of lectures. The professors were very good and engaging.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
MICR410 - Microbiota and Human Health
AE303A - Introduction to Ceramics Wheel and Hand Techniques
ES361 - The Biodiversity of British Columbia 
BIOL225 - Principles of Cell Biology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
MICR410 - Microbiota and Human Health
The professor was great and gave really good lectures, which made the course very interesting. There were two midterms, one larger assignment, and a final exam. Overall, it was a manageable course where I learned a lot.

AE303A - Introduction to Ceramics Wheel and Hand Techniques
I can definitely recommend this course. It was really nice to do something different from my science courses. The professor was great, and the classes were very enjoyable. However, there were quite a few deadlines, so it could be fairly demanding at times.

ES361 - The Biodiversity of British Columbia 
A really good course with a great professor. It was a relatively relaxed and manageable course, while still being very interesting and educational.

BIOL225 - Principles of Cell Biology
The course combined lectures with laboratory work, which worked really well and allowed me to learn a lot. There was an assignment after each lab, which helped make sure that we understood what we had been working on. However, it was quite a demanding course with several larger assignments.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I spent more money than expected on trips and travelling around the island. I would recommend setting aside a little more money than you initially expect to spend.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was more expensive than in Denmark, which surprised me a little.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were clubs for almost everything, so it was easy to find something interesting to take part in. I personally took figure skating classes, which were a lot of fun and a great way to meet people.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would definitely recommend joining some of the clubs or sports activities offered by the university. There are so many different options, so it is a great way to try something new and meet other students. I personally took figure skating classes, which I really enjoyed.
I would also recommend taking part in the social activities for exchange students. We often went to Lucky Bar on Mondays, where many exchange students would meet, went to hockey games, and visited board game cafés. It was a great way to meet people and be part of the social life in Victoria.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
I would definitely recommend exploring as much of Vancouver Island as possible. There are so many beautiful places to see and amazing hiking opportunities. One of my favourite trips was a road trip all the way up to Port Hardy and San Josef Bay, which was an amazing experience. I would also recommend visiting Tofino, where you can go surfing and explore the small and cosy town. At the end of our stay, we rented a big house there and went as a group of ten, which was a lot of fun.
There are also many great places to visit outside Vancouver Island. We went camping in Squamish, visited Vancouver, went skiing in Whistler, and took a trip to Forks in Washington, where we also camped.
I would also recommend going whale watching and exploring Victoria itself, as there are many nice areas, cafés, bakeries, and places to see. There are so many opportunities for weekend trips and adventures, so I would recommend exploring as much as possible while you are there!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy to adjust to the local culture. Everyone was incredibly friendly, helpful, and talkative, even more so than in Denmark, which made me feel very welcome from the beginning. People were always happy to help or have a conversation, and it made Victoria such a lovely place to arrive and settle into.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just be open and don’t be afraid to talk to new people! Most people are there for the same reason as you – to meet new people and have new experiences, so you quickly find a sense of comfort with each other. I would also recommend taking part in the social activities, especially during orientation week, as the university does a lot to help students meet and get to know each other.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn’t find any cultural differences particularly challenging. Overall, I found the culture quite similar to Denmark, and it was very easy to adjust. One difference I noticed was the strong awareness and respect for the Indigenous peoples and the traditional lands on which the university is located. This was something that was much more present than what I was used to in Denmark.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really appreciated how friendly, open, and helpful people were. People were very talkative and genuinely interested in meeting and talking to others, which created a very welcoming atmosphere. I also really appreciated the respect for nature and the outdoor lifestyle, as well as the awareness and respect for Indigenous peoples and their culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
First, be open and take part in as many social activities as possible, especially during orientation week. Everyone is there to meet new people and have new experiences.
Second, explore as much as you can! Vancouver Island and the surrounding areas have so much to offer, so make time for road trips, hiking, camping, surfing, skiing, and weekend trips. Some of my best memories from my exchange came from these experiences.
Third, start planning early and stay on top of deadlines, especially when it comes to course registration and housing. Some of the practical processes can be a little confusing and time-consuming, so it helps a lot to be well prepared.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would just say make the most of your time there! Victoria is an amazing place to study and live, and there are so many opportunities to meet new people, explore beautiful places, and try new things. Be open to new experiences and say yes to as much as you can. My exchange at UVic was an incredible experience, and I would definitely choose to go there again

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
The most rewarding part of my exchange was the whole experience of studying at UVic, meeting so many new people, and sharing so many amazing experiences with them. UVic was a great place to study, with really good professors and a beautiful campus. I especially loved the library and the overall atmosphere and surroundings on campus, which made it such a nice place to spend time.
Meeting people from different places and making new friendships was also a huge part of the experience. We got to explore so many new places and experience so many things together, which gave me memories and friendships that I will always value. Living and studying in a completely new country also pushed me out of my comfort zone and made me more confident and independent. Overall, it was an experience I will always remember.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge for me was meeting new people and speaking English, especially in front of the other Danish students. However, it quickly became easier, and by the end it felt completely natural

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Overall, I had an amazing exchange experience and would highly recommend UVic to future exchange students. Victoria is a great place to live and study, and I would definitely choose it again

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
